rationale:
bugs_open/423. A live, currently-reproducing defect with a root cause CONFIRMED at the code, by execution, and by a fleet census that could have come out otherwise. MECHANISM: buildServicesHTML (render_site_components_action.go, called at :125 to build the FOOTER services column) title-cases each word with `strings.ToUpper(w[:1]) + w[1:]`. That is a BYTE slice. strings.Fields makes a STANDALONE em-dash in a page title its own word, so w[:1] cuts a 3-byte rune after 1 byte: ToUpper of the lone lead byte yields U+FFFD and w[1:] re-attaches the orphaned continuation bytes. Ran it: "\u2014dash" -> ef bf bd 80 94, so the FIRST invalid byte is 0x80 — verbatim the byte in the live Postgres refusal captured on a chassis pod: `invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8": 0x80 (SQLSTATE 22021)`. Postgres REFUSES invalid UTF-8, so the footer UPDATE dies and the slot is never stored.

WHY IT WENT UNSEEN FOR TEN DAYS (the enabling defect, and the reason this is not a one-line patch): the store-failure branch logged the error and returned a NIL error, so the caller's chrome_render_failed map never heard it. The step completed SUCCESS with `rendered.footer=false` as its only trace, ineligible_chrome and locked_slots_preserved empty. Two sessions spent about an hour eliminating locks, component eligibility and empty content_data before a live pod-log capture named the actual refusal.

THE DISCRIMINATING CENSUS, stated because a weaker one was already run and did not discriminate. "The footer contains multi-byte characters" explains nothing: 32 of 32 stored footers contain them and all stored fine; the cause must CUT at a byte offset. Sites whose services-column labels (the query's own predicate, within its LIMIT 6) contain a word whose FIRST rune is multi-byte, 2026-09-02: exactly TWO — boxingonline.com and garden-tools.uk. Sites whose site_components footer is not build_status='rendered': exactly the SAME TWO. Every other footer on the fleet is 'rendered' with a matching digest. Zero false positives, zero false negatives. garden-tools.uk has been failing since 2026-08-23.

THE CLASS, not the case. Census of the idiom across non-test Go, 2026-09-02: EIGHT call sites, none rune-safe. The estate already fixed the TRUNCATION shape of this same class in 2026-07-20 (bugs_open/027 §4b, datahelpers.SafeCut) and never found the CASING shape — which is itself the argument for one shared primitive rather than a ninth hand-roll. So: datahelpers.UpperFirst, all 8 sites converted, ASCII parity pinned by test (that parity is what made a one-pass conversion safe).

AND THE DOOR-CLOSER, because fixing 8 sites does not stop the 9th. Postgres names the offending BYTE and never its POSITION, so a refusal on a 40 KB document says "0x80" and nothing about where; the only way to find out has been to bisect the pipeline by hand. A gate before the UPDATE reports the OFFSET plus a QuoteToASCII'd window (pure ASCII, so the report is itself storable — a diagnostic that cannot be persisted is a shape this very bug already contains). It REFUSES rather than sanitising: strings.ToValidUTF8 would make the store succeed, and this path has no gate downstream — whatever it stores is what the site serves (bugs_open/260) — so sanitising would ship silently mangled text over working chrome AND leave the upstream cut in place to keep producing it. Refusing keeps the previous bytes serving, which is the disposition this function already takes for every other bad render.

ONE THING I WANT THE SEATS TO PRESS ON: half 1 makes a store failure return a non-nil error, and the existing caller fails the STEP when the slot has nothing stored to serve. garden-tools.uk's footer rendered_html is NULL, so its next build now FAILS where it previously reported success. I believe that is correct and is exactly bugs_open/260's ruling applied consistently, but it is a real behaviour change on a live site and I would rather it were argued than assumed.

plan.summary: One shared rune-safe primitive replaces an 8-site hand-rolled byte slice that Postgres refuses; the chrome store's failure branch stops reporting a refusal as silence and takes the surface the execution-failure branch already has; and a pre-store gate names the byte offset Postgres will not, so the next byte-indexed slice upstream is attributable in one read instead of by bisection. Five tests, each mutation-proven red on 2026-09-02.

edits.symbol: UpperFirst + InvalidUTF8At (and this file's own converted call site)
edits.rationale:
The primitive. Upper-cases the FIRST RUNE, leaves the rest byte-identical, and returns already-invalid input untouched rather than substituting U+FFFD — this helper's job is not to CREATE the defect, and silently rewriting a caller's bad bytes would hide one a validator upstream should be naming. Placed beside SafeCut/TruncateString because they are the same class and a reader looking for one should find the other.

SAME FILE, also: InvalidUTF8At — The diagnostic Postgres does not give. Returns the byte offset of the first invalid sequence and a QuoteToASCII'd window (±48 bytes) around it. ASCII-only is deliberate and load-bearing: the report is logged, persisted and put in a work item summary, so a window carrying the raw bad bytes would reproduce the very defect it describes — which is precisely what the third edit below is about.

And this file's own instance of the idiom (:1980, in the display-name splitter) converted to UpperFirst, like the other seven.

edits.symbol: the live defect (:1622), half 1, the pre-store gate, the 3 truncations, and the emitter's phase
edits.rationale:
THE LIVE DEFECT: buildServicesHTML's word loop -> datahelpers.UpperFirst(w). Then four changes that belong in this one file and this one pass.

HALF 1 — bugs_open/423 half 1. A store that fails has exactly the disposition of a template that will not execute — previous bytes keep serving, and a site with nothing stored must not go live — so it takes the SAME surface built for bugs_open/260 rather than a second chrome-failure channel. The nil return was the enabling defect for the whole incident. NOTE THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: via the existing caller, a slot with nothing stored now fails the step.

THE THREE TRUNCATIONS (:1439, :1689, :1779) — The latent sibling, and it MUST land with the edit above rather than after it. emitChromeRenderFailedItem's summary interpolates an ARBITRARY error string; once the store-failure branch uses that emitter, a long error whose 248th byte falls inside a multi-byte character mints invalid UTF-8 and fails its own INSERT — the surface that REPORTS a chrome failure dying of the disease it reports, and silently, because every failure in that emitter is logged rather than returned. Uses datahelpers.SafeCut, the estate's existing truncation primitive (bugs_open/027 §4b); the 250-byte threshold is preserved exactly so no other behaviour moves.

THE GATE — The door-closer: fixing 8 call sites does not stop the 9th. REFUSE, not sanitise — argued in the rationale. Placed before the UPDATE so the report can carry an offset into the exact bytes that would have been stored, after every transform (RenderTemplate, DropDeadURLControls, injectBrandHeadTags) has run.

THE EMITTER'S PHASE — Reusing a surface means fixing its prose. Its operator-facing `fix` text said "this chrome component's template could not be executed" — false for two of its three callers now, and a queue entry that sends the next reader to the wrong half of the pipeline is the same class of defect as this bug. The phase reaches the summary and the spec; the item_key deliberately does NOT carry it, because a slot that is broken is one problem however far down the path it broke and a phase in the key would mint a second open item when the same slot failed differently on the next run.

edits.rationale: Two of the eight call sites, both deriving a site's LOGO TEXT from a name. Same byte slice, same failure: a company name beginning with a non-ASCII letter (an accented capital, a curly quote) is corrupted, and logo text is written to config and rendered into chrome — i.e. straight back at Postgres. Converted, not merely noted: leaving a known member of the class unfixed because it has not bitten yet is how the 2026-07-20 truncation fix missed the casing shape for six weeks.
The third logo-text derivation, in the render path itself. Same conversion, same reason as multipage_actions.go.
Call site 5 of 8. Converted in the same pass so the census can be re-run and come back clean.

Call site 6 of 8. HumaniseKey turns snake_case into a label; keys are ASCII today, so this one is a latent member rather than a live one — converted anyway, because the value of a class fix is that the next reader does not have to re-derive which members were safe. The eighth site, cmd/webdesignport/harvest.go:411, is converted identically and needed only an added datahelpers import; it is outside council scope so it has no edit of its own here.

Mutation-proven RED on 2026-09-02, not merely written. (1) UpperFirst reverted to the byte idiom -> invalid UTF-8, and the failure output literally reproduces the production bytes ef bf bd 80 94. (2) The same mutation kills a test built on boxingonline's REAL page title, split with strings.Fields exactly as the production loop does — the one test that fails on the actual production input. (3) ASCII parity with the old idiom, which is the claim that licensed converting eight sites at once. (4) An InvalidUTF8At that always reports clean -> red; it also asserts the window is pure ASCII, because a report that cannot itself be stored is useless at precisely this seam.

DRIVES the real emitter through sqlmock with a UTF-8-validating argument matcher on $6. Calling insertWorkItem with a prepared summary would pass regardless of what the emitter does — the vacuous-test trap cta_override_rejected_item_test.go documents in this same package. The input is built so the 247-byte cap lands INSIDE an em-dash, so reverting to the byte slice leaves the expectation unmet. Mutation-proven red 2026-09-02.

plan.risks:
BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, stated rather than buried: a chrome slot whose store fails and which has NOTHING stored to serve now fails the step, via the existing bugs_open/260 caller logic. garden-tools.uk's footer rendered_html is NULL, so this is not hypothetical — its next build fails where it previously reported success. I hold that this is 260's ruling applied consistently (a site must not go live with a missing footer) and that a build failing loudly beats ten more days of silence, but it is the edit I most want argued.

The gate REFUSES invalid UTF-8 rather than sanitising it. If a future producer legitimately needs lossy repair, this is the wrong place for it — the repair belongs at the producer, and the gate is what will name the producer.

The 8-site conversion is behaviour-preserving only on ASCII, which is pinned by test. On non-ASCII input the output CHANGES — from corrupt to correct. Any downstream consumer that had come to depend on the corrupted form would break; I know of none, and such a consumer could not have round-tripped through Postgres.

Go, so INERT until the next image build and roll. The two casualty sites stay broken until then; boxingonline.com's served footer is a hand patch meanwhile.
